## old_workflow
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # This workspace bumps interdependent Cargo packages together, so a
          # bumped member's own Cargo.lock entry goes stale without this --
          # see ARCHITECTURE.md's "Lockfile Staleness" section.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          # include-hidden-files: upload-artifact excludes dotfiles by
          # default, and .release-handoff is one -- without this it silently
          # uploads nothing and "execute" downloads an empty artifact.
          include-hidden-files: true
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}

          # credentials: dispatch_tag (callisto-graph) pushes the release tag
          # with a plain `git push`, which has no other way to authenticate.
          # This job's own contents: write permission (above) is what backs it.
          persist-credentials: true
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          # .release-handoff and release-artifacts were sibling upload paths

GitHub documents that reruns retain the original event’s `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF`; this run is still bound to merge commit `0e0016e`, whose workflow downloads artifacts into `.release-intent` and `.release-build`. The waiting job therefore has the same precondition violation that already caused E051. Do not approve that pending deployment yet.

I’m continuing the code-path audit now, especially for sibling instances of the same “workflow passes unit/contract checks but violates runtime trust” class and for whether the current pipeline has any legitimate way to recover an already-versioned release.

1 # Publishing with Callisto
   2 
   3 This document covers authentication setup for registry publishing, with particular attention
   4 to npm, where there are two distinct auth patterns and common points of confusion.
   5 
   6 ---
   7 
   8 ## Repository durable-release workflow
   9 
  10 Callisto's own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` separates release work into four
  11 authority boundaries. A push with pending changesets creates or updates the release PR. That
  12 PR versions manifests and changelogs and removes only the changesets it consumed. Nothing is
  13 removed from `main` until that PR is merged.
  14 
  15 The normal GitHub flow keeps one `callisto/version-packages` release PR and recomputes it from
  16 the current base branch whenever changesets land. This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a
  17 literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or
  18 changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward. The action never runs a local `git push`
  19 to update that branch. Instead it stages the recomputed change as a commit rooted at the
  20 current `main` via GitHub's `createCommitOnBranch` commit API, restricted to non-workflow
  21 paths so `.github/workflows/*` is always inherited unchanged from the branch's current tip,
  22 then moves the release branch's ref onto that commit with a plain REST ref update. GitHub's
  23 built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/*` through the Git push protocol or
  24 through `createCommitOnBranch`'s own file changes on a public repository, but a ref move that
  25 carries no workflow-file write is not subject to that restriction, so the built-in token never
  26 needs elevated permission to keep the branch current. The resulting commits are GitHub-signed
  27 ("Verified") and attributed to `github-actions[bot]`. Repositories that already have a
  28 SHA-suffixed branch and PR from before this change (created under the prior fallback behavior)
  29 do not need to migrate anything -- that branch is a normal, continuously-updated managed branch
  30 going forward. An optional App or fine-grained token remains available for repositories that
  31 want release PR operations attributed to a different identity, but is never required.
  32 
  33 After a merge, the workflow derives a transient release intent from the signed merge commit's
  34 actual delta, builds from that exact commit, and passes the intent between jobs as a same-run
  35 GitHub artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. It is not committed and it is never recovered from a
  36 cache. The execute job rechecks the handoff before calling `callisto release execute`.
  37 
  38 Create a GitHub Environment named `release` before enabling registry credentials. Configure
  39 at least one required reviewer and appropriate branch/tag deployment rules in the repository's
  40 Environment settings. The workflow queries the Environment API and fails if the reviewer rule
  41 is absent; the `environment: release` job boundary is what prevents registry secrets from being
  42 available to planning or build jobs.
  43 
  44 An administrator must also enable a branch-protection rule or ruleset on `main` that requires
  45 CODEOWNERS review. [`.github/CODEOWNERS`](../.github/CODEOWNERS) names the real owner for
  46 workflow and action changes, but GitHub does not enforce review merely because that file exists.
  47 
  48 Only the `execute` job may receive `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, or `TWINE_PASSWORD`.
  49 Do not put those secrets at workflow scope, in build jobs, or in an action input. Binary releases
  50 add exact files plus `release-artifacts/manifest.json` to the build handoff; their GitHub build
  51 attestations are verified by Callisto before upload. Source-only releases do not need that
  52 manifest.
  53 
  54 `callisto-action` is now a compatibility version-PR action only. Its former `publish` and
  55 `create_github_release` inputs are ignored; it never publishes, tags, downloads artifacts, or
  56 creates a forge release. The repository durable workflow is the supported release path.
  57 
  58 ---
  59 
  60 ## npm Registry Authentication
  61 
  62 Callisto delegates all npm publishing to the `npm` or `pnpm` CLI (see the coordinator
  63 pattern in `00-design.md` §11.1 and §9). This means callisto never reads NPM credentials
  64 directly — whatever auth the npm CLI can see when it runs is what gets used. There are two
  65 supported patterns.
  66 
  67 ---
  68 
  69 ### Pattern A: Manual `.npmrc` setup via `NPM_TOKEN`
  70 
  71 Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret in your repository. Add this only in the protected `execute`
  72 job, immediately before the command that publishes:
  73 
  74 ```yaml
  75 - name: Authenticate with npm registry
  76   run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  77   env:
  78     NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
  79 
  80 - run: callisto release execute --intent .release-intent/release-intent.json
  81 ```
  82 
  83 This works because `npm config set` writes to the user-level `.npmrc`, which the npm CLI
  84 reads for every subsequent publish call in the same job.
  85 
  86 The version-PR action never receives this token. It only creates or updates a reviewed PR.
  87 
  88 ---
  89 
  90 ### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
  91 
  92 `actions/setup-node` has built-in npm auth support: when you pass `registry-url`, it writes
  93 a project-level `.npmrc` configured to read the token from the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` environment
  94 variable. Set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in the job environment:
  95 
  96 ```yaml
  97 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  98   with:
  99     node-version: '20'
 100     registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
 101 
 102 - run: callisto release execute --intent .release-intent/release-intent.json
 103   env:
 104     NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
 105 ```
 106 
 107 **How this works:** `actions/setup-node` writes an `.npmrc` file containing a line like:
 108 `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. The npm CLI evaluates this shell
 109 expansion at publish time, picking up the environment variable. Without the `.npmrc` entry
 110 written by `setup-node`, setting `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` alone has no effect — npm does not read
 111 that variable unless a corresponding `.npmrc` line tells it to.
 112 
 113 **Warning:** `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` is silently ignored by npm if no `.npmrc` contains a
 114 `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` interpolation. If you set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in your workflow but did
 115 not also run `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` set, your publish will fail with an
 116 authentication error — not a variable-not-found error, because npm never reads the variable
 117 in that case.
 118 
 119 ---
 120 
 121 ### Choosing a pattern
 122 
 123 | Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
 124 |---|---|---|
 125 | Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
 126 | Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
 127 | Recommended when | Your execute job does not otherwise need Node setup | Your execute job already uses `setup-node` |
 128 | Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
 129 
 130 If your execute job already calls `actions/setup-node` and sets `registry-url`, Pattern B
 131 works because `setup-node` wrote the `.npmrc`. Do not add `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` to a job that
 132 does not run `setup-node` with `registry-url`.
 133 
 134 ---
 135 
 136 ## npm Platform/Main Package Publishing
 137 
 138 A napi-rs (or maturin) native package publishes as **N platform-specific packages** — one
 139 per target triple, e.g. `my-lib-linux-x64-gnu`, `my-lib-darwin-arm64` — plus **one main
 140 package** that end users actually install. The main package's `optionalDependencies` pin
 141 exact versions of every platform sibling; npm resolves whichever one matches the installer's
 142 OS/arch at install time. See `00-design.md` §5.3 and §7.5 for how platform packages are
 143 detected from `napi.targets`/`[tool.maturin].targets`.
 144 
 145 ### Publish order
 146 
 147 `callisto publish` publishes in this fixed order: Rust crates → npm platform packages → npm
 148 main packages → PyPI packages. Platform packages always publish before the main package that
 149 depends on them.
 150 
 151 ### What happens when a platform package fails
 152 
 153 If a platform package fails to publish in the same run, its dependent main package is
 154 **skipped, not attempted** — publishing it anyway would ship `optionalDependencies` pointing
 155 at a version that was never uploaded. The skipped entry appears in the publish report as:
 156 
 157 ```json
 158 {
 159   "package": "npm/my-lib",
 160   "status": "failed",
 161   "errorKind": "dependencyFailed",
 162   "error": "skipped: platform dependency failed to publish: my-lib-linux-x64-gnu"
 163 }
 164 ```
 165 
 166 `dependencyFailed` means exactly this — the main package was never attempted, because a
 167 declared platform dependency failed to publish *in this same run*. It is not itself a
 168 registry error. **Remediation:** fix whatever made the platform package fail, then re-run
 169 `callisto publish` — it is idempotent and will skip anything already uploaded.
 170 
 171 ### What happens when a platform dependency is missing entirely
 172 
 173 Before any registry call is made, `callisto plan-publish` cross-checks every main package's
 174 declared platform dependencies against what actually ended up in the plan. A dependency is
 175 allowed to be absent only if it's already published (its on-disk version already matches its
 176 last release tag). Otherwise — a misconfigured platform package with no npm publish target,
 177 or one excluded via `--package` — planning fails outright with a `MissingPlatformDependency`
 178 error naming the main package and the missing dependency, before anything is published.
 179 
 180 ---
 181 
 182 ## Cargo (crates.io) Authentication
 183 
 184 Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment.
 185 `cargo publish` reads it directly:
 186 
 187 ```yaml
 188 env:
 189   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
 190 ```
 191 
 192 No `.cargo/credentials` setup step is needed; cargo recognizes the environment variable
 193 natively.
 194 
 195 ---
 196 
 197 ## Python (PyPI) Authentication
 198 
 199 Python publishing uses `twine upload`. Twine reads credentials from two environment
 200 variables: `TWINE_USERNAME` (set to `__token__` when using a PyPI API token) and
 201 `TWINE_PASSWORD` (set to the API token value). Set these in the job environment before
 202 the Callisto release action runs:
 203 
 204 ```yaml
 205 env:
 206   TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
 207   TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
 208 ```
 209 
 210 Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognise that variable name.
 211 
 212 ---
 213 
 214 ## Full workflow example with npm auth (Pattern A)
 215 
 216 This extends the Paradigm 1 example from `release-paradigms.md` to include npm publishing:
 217 
 218 ```yaml
 219 name: Release & Publish Workflow
 220 
 221 on:
 222   push:
 223     branches:
 224       - main
 225   workflow_dispatch:
 226 
 227 concurrency:
 228   group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
 229   cancel-in-progress: false
 230 
 231 jobs:
 232   verify:
 233     name: Verify CI Pipeline
 234     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 235     steps:
 236       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 237         with:
 238           fetch-depth: 0
 239       - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
 240       - run: moon run :format-check
 241       - run: moon run :lint
 242       - run: moon run :test
 243 
 244   release:
 245     name: Version Packages or Publish Release
 246     needs: [verify]
 247     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 248     permissions:
 249       contents: write
 250       pull-requests: write
 251     steps:
 252       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 253         with:
 254           fetch-depth: 0
 255           token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
 256       - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
 257       - uses: ./.github/actions/callisto-action
 258         # This action only creates or updates the release PR. Registry tokens
 259         # belong exclusively in the protected execute job after merge.
 260 ```

 142 OS/arch at install time. See `00-design.md` §5.3 and §7.5 for how platform packages are
 143 detected from `napi.targets`/`[tool.maturin].targets`.
 144

 146 
 147 `callisto publish` publishes in this fixed order: Rust crates → npm platform packages → npm
 148 main packages → PyPI packages. Platform packages always publish before the main package that
 149 depends on them.
 150

 152 
 153 If a platform package fails to publish in the same run, its dependent main package is
 154 **skipped, not attempted** — publishing it anyway would ship `optionalDependencies` pointing
 155 at a version that was never uploaded. The skipped entry appears in the publish report as:
 156 
 157 ```json

 159   "package": "npm/my-lib",
 160   "status": "failed",
 161   "errorKind": "dependencyFailed",
 162   "error": "skipped: platform dependency failed to publish: my-lib-linux-x64-gnu"
 163 }
 164 ```
 165

 167 declared platform dependency failed to publish *in this same run*. It is not itself a
 168 registry error. **Remediation:** fix whatever made the platform package fail, then re-run
 169 `callisto publish` — it is idempotent and will skip anything already uploaded.
 170 
 171 ### What happens when a platform dependency is missing entirely
 172 
 173 Before any registry call is made, `callisto plan-publish` cross-checks every main package's
 174 declared platform dependencies against what actually ended up in the plan. A dependency is
 175 allowed to be absent only if it's already published (its on-disk version already matches its
 176 last release tag). Otherwise — a misconfigured platform package with no npm publish target,
 177 or one excluded via `--package` — planning fails outright with a `MissingPlatformDependency`
 178 error naming the main package and the missing dependency, before anything is published.
 179

1 # Publishing with Callisto
   2 
   3 This document covers authentication setup for registry publishing, with particular attention
   4 to npm, where there are two distinct auth patterns and common points of confusion.
   5 
   6 ---
   7 
   8 ## Repository durable-release workflow
   9 
  10 Callisto's own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` separates release work into four
  11 authority boundaries. A push with pending changesets creates or updates the release PR. That
  12 PR versions manifests and changelogs and removes only the changesets it consumed. Nothing is
  13 removed from `main` until that PR is merged.
  14 
  15 The normal GitHub flow keeps one `callisto/version-packages` release PR and recomputes it from
  16 the current base branch whenever changesets land. This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a
  17 literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or
  18 changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward. The action never runs a local `git push`
  19 to update that branch. Instead it stages the recomputed change as a commit rooted at the
  20 current `main` via GitHub's `createCommitOnBranch` commit API, restricted to non-workflow
  21 paths so `.github/workflows/*` is always inherited unchanged from the branch's current tip,
  22 then moves the release branch's ref onto that commit with a plain REST ref update. GitHub's
  23 built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/*` through the Git push protocol or
  24 through `createCommitOnBranch`'s own file changes on a public repository, but a ref move that
  25 carries no workflow-file write is not subject to that restriction, so the built-in token never
  26 needs elevated permission to keep the branch current. The resulting commits are GitHub-signed
  27 ("Verified") and attributed to `github-actions[bot]`. Repositories that already have a
  28 SHA-suffixed branch and PR from before this change (created under the prior fallback behavior)
  29 do not need to migrate anything -- that branch is a normal, continuously-updated managed branch
  30 going forward. An optional App or fine-grained token remains available for repositories that
  31 want release PR operations attributed to a different identity, but is never required.
  32 
  33 After a merge, the workflow derives a transient release intent from the signed merge commit's
  34 actual delta, builds from that exact commit, and passes the intent between jobs as a same-run
  35 GitHub artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. It is not committed and it is never recovered from a
  36 cache. The execute job rechecks the handoff before calling `callisto release execute`.
  37 
  38 Create a GitHub Environment named `release` before enabling registry credentials. Configure
  39 at least one required reviewer and appropriate branch/tag deployment rules in the repository's
  40 Environment settings. The workflow queries the Environment API and fails if the reviewer rule
  41 is absent; the `environment: release` job boundary is what prevents registry secrets from being
  42 available to planning or build jobs.

  44 An administrator must also enable a branch-protection rule or ruleset on `main` that requires
  45 CODEOWNERS review. [`.github/CODEOWNERS`](../.github/CODEOWNERS) names the real owner for
  46 workflow and action changes, but GitHub does not enforce review merely because that file exists.
  47 
  48 Only the `execute` job may receive `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, or `TWINE_PASSWORD`.
  49 Do not put those secrets at workflow scope, in build jobs, or in an action input. Binary releases
  50 add exact files plus `release-artifacts/manifest.json` to the build handoff; their GitHub build
  51 attestations are verified by Callisto before upload. Source-only releases do not need that
  52 manifest.

  55 `create_github_release` inputs are ignored; it never publishes, tags, downloads artifacts, or
  56 creates a forge release. The repository durable workflow is the supported release path.

  59 
  60 ## npm Registry Authentication
  61 
  62 Callisto delegates all npm publishing to the `npm` or `pnpm` CLI (see the coordinator

  65 supported patterns.

  84 reads for every subsequent publish call in the same job.

 114 `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` interpolation. If you set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in your workflow but did
 115 not also run `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` set, your publish will fail with an

 117 in that case.

1 {
   2   "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-012",
   3   "status": "draft",
   4   "owner_track": "release-security",
   5   "last_verified_revision": "289001ec",
   6   "depends_on": [
   7     "SPEC-RELEASE-INTENT-MODEL-009",
   8     "SPEC-RELEASE-TRUST-010",
   9     "SPEC-RELEASE-CAPABILITY-011"
  10   ],
  11   "purpose": "Execute one freshly validated release intent safely across registries, Git tags, and forge releases. Execution records durable progress before each effect, recovers by observing exact provider identities, and accepts compiled binaries only through an intent-bound artifact manifest plus a verified GitHub artifact attestation.",
  12   "scope": "The provider-neutral execution coordinator, durable state and terminal receipt, state storage, reconciliation, artifact-manifest validation, and provider observation/effect adapter contracts. It consumes the approved decision, typed intent, Git trust evidence, and ValidatedReleaseIntent defined by its dependencies. It does not define the CLI or GitHub Actions invocation surfaces; SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013 owns those.",
  13   "non_goals": [
  14     "Distributed transactions, rollback of a completed registry publication, or parallel remote effects.",
  15     "Publishing, tagging, or creating a forge release from PublishPlan, PublishReport, inline configuration, a cache entry, mutable workspace configuration, or a caller-computed provider target.",
  16     "Persisting credentials, raw registry endpoints, request headers, command lines, provider stderr, arbitrary error text, miette reports, or raw configuration bytes in execution state, receipts, or artifact manifests.",
  17     "Supporting non-Git or non-detached source trust in version 1.",
  18     "Using Rayon or Tokio to parallelize lock-held, ordered release effects."
  19   ],
  20   "terms": {
  21     "terminal_success": "A role-specific observation proves the exact intended effect exists, or an adapter has just completed that effect and observed it. It is not inferred from the absence of a failure.",
  22     "terminal_non_success": "A closed, credential-free failure or operator-required outcome. It prevents dependent operations from dispatching.",
  23     "prepared_operation": "Graph-private, operation-specific input retained by ValidatedReleaseIntent during fresh validation. It is the only source from which an adapter may construct an effect request.",
  24     "artifact_slot": "A typed output requested by an intent for a compiled binary release, including its package/version/platform/role identity and GitHub attestation policy but never arbitrary user file paths.",
  25     "reconcile": "A read-only report over current state and exact provider observations. It never writes state and never changes an operation status. `release execute --resume` owns any permitted state transition after presenting the same evidence."
  26   },
  27   "acceptance_criteria": [
  28     {
  29       "id": "AC-001",
  30       "criterion": "ReleaseExecutionStateV1 is an intent-bound, credential-free record with exactly one state entry for every operation in ReleaseIntentV1's canonical DAG. New execution initializes every entry as Pending. Before any remote or VCS effect for an operation, the coordinator changes that entry to Attempting and atomically persists a complete parseable state file. Only after the adapter returns and its role-specific postcondition has been observed may the entry become a terminal outcome. State transitions are monotonic: Pending -> Attempting -> terminal, with no terminal-to-pending rewrite and no second attempt of a terminal-success operation. A crash after the Attempting write and before or during the provider call is therefore distinguishable from an operation that was never started.",
  31       "is_error_case": true
  32     },
  33     {
  34       "id": "AC-002",
  35       "criterion": "State storage has an explicit path override and a safe local default. Without an override, Callisto derives a platform application-state location from the canonical repository root and IntentDigest; it never creates release state in the checkout. CI and advanced callers may provide an explicit path. Every write uses callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write and includes the matching schema/version and intent digest. An existing state file whose schema, intent digest, operation roster, or immutable operation identity differs from the supplied intent is rejected before any effect. State may be uploaded/downloaded as a workflow artifact, but a cache is never authority for state or intent.",
  36       "is_error_case": true
  37     },
  38     {
  39       "id": "AC-003",
  40       "criterion": "Reconciliation is observation-driven and never treats `no recorded failure`, `Attempting`, `Pending`, a missing receipt, or an HTTP success from a different identity as success. `release reconcile` is read-only: Pending remains Pending; only an Attempting operation may be reported as proven-success, conflicting, ambiguous, or still-unproven. `release execute --resume` alone may persist the matching legal result after the same observation. Version 1 performs no automatic retry. A terminal non-success prevents dependent operations and requires an operator to create a fresh release attempt under a separately specified retry policy; it is never silently retried. Dependent operations are eligible only when every declared prerequisite is terminal success. Thus an interruption cannot allow tag or forge-release operations to run because unattempted publishes merely lack failures.",
  41       "is_error_case": true
  42     },
  43     {
  44       "id": "AC-004",
  45       "criterion": "The coordinator dispatches effects in the intent's canonical topological order while retaining the workspace release lock from final capability validation through the last state/receipt persistence. Before each dispatch it rechecks the Git trust evidence, intent binding, artifact binding when applicable, and prerequisite terminal-success states while holding that lock. A changed HEAD, non-detached checkout, dirty tree, missing/mismatched prepared operation, stale intent, or failed prerequisite aborts before that effect. The lock coordinates Callisto processes; the rechecks protect against external writers and provider races.",
  46       "is_error_case": true
  47     },
  48     {
  49       "id": "AC-005",
  50       "criterion": "Provider adapters accept only (&ValidatedReleaseIntent, &ApplyPermit, OperationId) or a narrower internal capability derived from those values; they do not accept PublishPlan, free-form package/version/URL/tag arguments, or mutable workspace config. A registry observation/effect is keyed by the exact ReleasePackageId, target version, and RegistryBindingId. A Git tag observation/effect verifies the exact tag name, target commit, annotated-versus-lightweight policy, and required annotation policy. A forge-release observation/effect verifies the exact forge binding and tag/target identity. An identity collision, an already-existing object with different metadata, or an ambiguous provider response is a safe non-success outcome, never an idempotent success.",
  51       "is_error_case": true
  52     },
  53     {
  54       "id": "AC-006",
  55       "criterion": "ArtifactManifestV1 is a typed, credential-free build output bound to exactly one IntentDigest and the intent's exact source commit. It contains one entry for each required artifact slot and, for each entry, the declared slot identity, normalized platform/role, raw-byte SHA-256 ArtifactDigest, byte length, and safe GitHub attestation locator/subject digest. Before any binary forge-upload operation, the executor validates the manifest's schema, intent digest, source commit, complete unique slot roster, and downloaded bytes; it then verifies the exact downloaded bytes with GitHub artifact-attestation verification, pins the intent's configured repository and immutable signer workflow, and checks the verified provenance statement's source commit against the intent. A signature alone, a matching byte digest alone, or an attestation from another repository/workflow/source commit is insufficient. Missing, duplicate, unexpected, wrong-platform, wrong-version, wrong-source, digest-mismatched, unattested, or policy-mismatched assets block the relevant operation. Version 1 rejects binary slots outside this GitHub-attested path; source registry publishing remains a distinct operation and does not consume or imply a compiled-binary artifact.",
  56       "is_error_case": true
  57     },
  58     {
  59       "id": "AC-007",
  60       "criterion": "After every operation reaches a terminal outcome, the coordinator persists state before evaluating the next operation. A ReleaseReceiptV1 is written only after every operation is terminal success and after final source/intent binding rechecks; it records the intent digest, safe terminal evidence, and receipt schema/version. A partially completed or non-successful release has state but no successful terminal receipt. Receipt creation is idempotent only for byte-equivalent receipt identity; a mismatched existing receipt is rejected.",
  61       "is_error_case": true
  62     },
  63     {
  64       "id": "AC-008",
  65       "criterion": "All persisted outcome/error fields are closed enums and fixed safe identifiers. User-facing failures use miette diagnostics with actionable remediation, but diagnostics are transient and never serialized as durable evidence. Tests cover interruption immediately before a provider call, immediately after a provider-side success but before terminal persistence, already-existing exact identity, already-existing conflicting identity, stale state, changed Git evidence, artifact-manifest substitution, and an unattempted prerequisite; each test asserts no unauthorized dependent effect dispatches.",
  66       "is_error_case": true
  67     }
  68   ],
  69   "implementation_notes": [
  70     "callisto-graph owns the ReleaseCoordinator and provider observation/effect adapter traits. callisto-vcs owns only the Git trust/effect adapter. callisto-cli assembles adapters and maps diagnostics; it does not own release policy or state transitions.",
  71     "Keep provider-specific HTTP/Git/GitHub clients behind narrow adapters. Their observation result should be a typed proof or a closed safe non-success result, not a boolean and not a stringly typed response. The GitHub artifact adapter must use the platform's cryptographic verification semantics, not merely download an attestation record or compare an unverified JSON field.",
  72     "The durable model may hold RegistryBindingId and ArtifactDigest, while endpoint parsing/canonicalization and provider clients remain in graph/effect-layer crates so Layer 1 does not gain network/config dependencies.",
  73     "The whole-state atomic rewrite is intentionally preferred to an append-only log at workspace-release scale: interruption readers always receive a complete parseable file."
  74   ],
  75   "revision_note": "Split from umbrella SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-FOUNDATION-007 after adversarial review established that prepared authority, recovery evidence, and binary artifacts need explicit contracts before real effects are introduced."
  76 }

1 {
   2   "id": "SPEC-TRACK4-RELEASE-PIPELINE-CONTRACT-CORRECTNESS",
   3   "purpose": "Correct four confirmed-live correctness bugs in the release pipeline's CLI-to-Action contract so the shipped GitHub Action reliably reaches release-PR-creation and publish on real runs, instead of erroring out on the normal 'pending changesets' case or silently reporting fabricated state (a stale tag sha, a missing changelog excerpt) -- in both apply mode and `--dry-run` preview mode.",
   4   "scope": "Four fixes, all within the callisto CLI/graph crates and the composite Action script: (1) .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml's `callisto status --check` exit-code branching in the 'Inspecting Workspace Status' step, including the unrecognised-exit-code path (0 included); (2) crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs's top-of-file exit-code-contract doc comment for the `status` subcommand; (3) crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs's `create_tags_with_options`, specifically the `sha` field written into the `CreatedTag` pushed for the per-release tag, in both the apply path (permit granted, tag.rs:82-117) and the `--dry-run` preview path (permit is None, tag.rs:53-80); (4) crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs's `plan_publish`, specifically the `changelog_section` field on `ReleaseEntry` (currently hardcoded `None`), which must be populated via `callisto_changelog::extract_section` (crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs:102) reading the package's already-resolved changelog file at `pkg.changelog` (`Package.changelog: Option<PathBuf>`, always `Some`, workspace-root-relative -- the same field `callisto version`'s changelog-rendering step already uses at commands/version.rs:148, honoring any `[[package]] changelog = \"...\"` override), plus the two new `DiagnosticCode` cases that surface non-fatal changelog conditions.",
   5   "non_goals": [
   6     "Track 6-mechanical's JSON report field-shape mismatches (StatusReport, StatusPackageRecord, SnapshotReport, ComposePrBodyReport, CreatedTag's other fields, InitReport, ValidateReport) -- separate track, not touched here.",
   7     "Any change to callisto-model's SCHEMA_VERSION constant or any report type's struct fields -- all four fixes reuse existing fields (CreatedTag.sha, ReleaseEntry.changelog_section) or correct logic/prose; the one addition (a new DiagnosticCode variant for AC-12c) extends an already-`#[non_exhaustive]` enum additively and does not require a version bump under this project's current pre-first-publish posture (no real external consumer of this wire format exists yet).",
   8     "The `callisto publish` command's actual registry-publishing logic (cargo/npm/pypi clients) -- untouched.",
   9     "Any change to how the Action script parses `plan-publish`'s or `matrix`'s JSON output via `jq`, beyond the status-check exit-code branching fix -- those jq parse sites are already confirmed working and out of scope.",
  10     "Adding a dedicated CLI flag or new exit code to distinguish clap usage errors (exit 2) from 'no changesets pending' (exit 2) at the `callisto` binary level -- clap's own exit-code convention is not renegotiated by this track; the fix for the collision lives entirely in the Action script's ability to tell the two apart, not by changing what the CLI emits.",
  11     "Any change to `callisto status`'s non-`--check` (plain) exit-code behavior -- confirmed correct already (0 on success regardless of pending changesets, 1 on error); only the `--check` branch and its doc comment are in scope.",
  12     "Resolving what `changelog_section` should contain when a package has a CHANGELOG.md with malformed markdown (e.g. no `##` headings at all) -- that is the documented 'heading not found' case already covered by AC-12.",
  13     "The floating-major alias tag's CreatedTag.sha (tag.rs:99-107 apply path, tag.rs:64-69 dry-run path) -- this is NOT the same bug class as the per-release tag. `create_floating_major` is called unconditionally on every apply run regardless of the alias's prior existence or target (tag.rs:102, no `already_existed`-style gate), so `release.sha` is deterministically what the alias becomes after any real apply run -- there is no 'different real answer' being hidden, unlike the per-release tag which is genuinely left unmoved when it already exists. Reporting `release.sha` for the floating-major alias in BOTH apply mode (where it is now true by construction) and `--dry-run` mode (where it accurately previews what the unconditional apply step will produce) is therefore correct as-is and out of scope for this fix."
  14   ],
  15   "api_surface": [
  16     {
  17       "name": "check_exit_code_raw",
  18       "signature": "fn check_exit_code_raw(report: &StatusReport) -> u8 (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:18)",
  19       "description": "Already-correct, unchanged by this spec: returns 1 when any package has a non-empty pending_changesets list, 2 otherwise. `handle` (status.rs:53-54) returns ExitCode::from(this value) when --check is set and there are no diagnostic errors. This is the ground truth the Action script and the main.rs doc comment must both agree with."
  20     },
  21     {
  22       "name": "create_tags_with_options",
  23       "signature": "fn create_tags_with_options<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, plan: &PublishPlan, opts: &TagOptions, permit: Option<&ApplyPermit>) -> Result<TagReport, GraphError> (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:30)",
  24       "description": "Two structurally parallel paths must both use the same already-existing-tag detection and sha resolution for the PER-RELEASE tag only (not the floating-major alias, see non_goals): the apply path (permit is Some, tag.rs:82-117) currently checks `ws.tags()?.contains_tag(tag_str)` (tag.rs:82) to decide whether to call `git.create_tag`, but unconditionally pushes `CreatedTag { sha: release.sha.clone(), .. }` (tag.rs:113-117) regardless of that check's outcome; the dry-run path (permit is None, tag.rs:53-80) currently performs NO existence check at all and unconditionally pushes `release.sha` (tag.rs:74-78). Both paths must be fixed identically: when the per-release tag already exists at a commit different from `release.sha`, the reported `sha` must be the tag's real current target via `GitDataSource::resolve_commit(&self, refname: &str) -> Result<Option<CommitSha>, VcsError>` (crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs:79, reachable via `ws.git_access()`, tag.rs:48) -- not `release.sha` -- in BOTH modes; the dry-run path must perform this check and lookup without mutating any git state (no `git.create_tag` call, matching its existing preview-only contract). When `resolve_commit` returns `Ok(None)` or `Err(VcsError)` for an already-existing tag, in either mode, `create_tags_with_options` must return `Err(GraphError)` immediately (fail-fast, e.g. via `GraphError::Vcs` for the `Err` case and an explicit error construction for the `Ok(None)` case) rather than falling back to `release.sha` -- consistent with this function's existing git-access-failure handling and with this spec's purpose of never fabricating reported state, in a preview or otherwise."
  25     },
  26     {
  27       "name": "extract_section",
  28       "signature": "fn extract_section<'a>(changelog: &'a str, version: &Version) -> Option<&'a str> (crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs:102)",
  29       "description": "Already-implemented and already-unit-tested. Finds the `## {version}` heading in `changelog` and returns the slice of content between that heading and the next `## ` heading (or end of file), trimmed, or `None` if the heading is not found OR the matched section's trimmed content is empty (write.rs:131-136: `if raw_section.is_empty() { None } else { Some(raw_section) }`). `plan_publish` must call this with the content of the package's resolved changelog file at `pkg.changelog` (crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:17, `Option<PathBuf>` but always `Some` by construction -- populated in walk.rs:387-392 as either a `[[package]] changelog = \"...\"` override path or the default co-located `CHANGELOG.md`, workspace-root-relative) and `ver` (the release version) -- the identical field `plan_version` already reads at commands/version.rs:148 to decide where to render changelog entries, so the read and write sides always agree on which file is 'the' changelog for a package. Three distinct non-fatal outcomes, each leaving `changelog_section` as `None` and never erroring or panicking the whole plan: (a) no file exists yet at the `pkg.changelog` path (AC-11) -- the common case before a package's first release, since `callisto version` creates the file on first write, (b) file exists but `extract_section` returns `None` -- no matching heading, or a matching heading with empty content (AC-12) -- both add a `DiagnosticCode::ChangelogSectionNotFound` (crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs, already exists, currently reserved/unemitted) diagnostic at Warning severity naming the package, (c) file exists but fails to read as valid UTF-8 or fails for a reason other than not-found (AC-12c) -- adds a NEW `DiagnosticCode::ChangelogReadError` variant (Warning severity) naming the package and the read failure."
  30     }
  31   ],
  32   "acceptance_criteria": [
  33     {
  34       "id": "AC-01",
  35       "criterion": "In .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml's 'Inspecting Workspace Status' step, when `callisto status --check` exits with code 1 (the documented 'pending changesets' contract), the script sets HAS_CHANGESETS=true and proceeds into the release-PR-creation branch (the `if [[ \"$HAS_CHANGESETS\" == \"true\" ]]` block), rather than falling through to the unexpected-exit-code branch. Verifiable by reading the script's if/elif/else chain against this exit-code table, or by replacing the `callisto status --check` invocation with a stub that exits 1 and observing which branch's echo output appears.",
  36       "is_error_case": false
  37     },
  38     {
  39       "id": "AC-02",
  40       "criterion": "In the same step, when `callisto status --check` exits with code 2 (the documented 'no changesets pending' contract), the script sets HAS_CHANGESETS=false and proceeds into the publish branch (the `else` arm of `if [[ \"$HAS_CHANGESETS\" == \"true\" ]]`). Verifiable the same way as AC-01, substituting an exit-2 stub.",
  41       "is_error_case": false
  42     },
  43     {
  44       "id": "AC-04",

   2   "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-TRUST-010",
   3   "status": "draft",
   4   "owner_track": "release-security",
   5   "last_verified_revision": "289001ec",
   6   "depends_on": [
   7     "SPEC-RELEASE-DECISION-008",
   8     "SPEC-RELEASE-INTENT-MODEL-009"
   9   ],
  10   "purpose": "Define the Git-only source-trust and workspace-exclusion contract used by version-1 durable releases. It turns the approved source commit into freshly observed, non-durable trust evidence and prevents two Callisto release processes from validating or effecting the same workspace concurrently.",
  11   "scope": "Fresh Git observation, canonical workspace-root binding, clean detached-HEAD policy, local release locking, and re-observation rules. This does not define release policy, durable intent fields, graph preparation, provider effects, or a non-Git release mode.",
  12   "non_goals": [
  13     "Supporting branch, symbolic-HEAD, dirty-worktree, non-Git, HermeticContent, or SHA-256 Git-object-format execution in version 1.",
  14     "Using a Git SHA as evidence of human authorship, signature verification, or forge authorization.",
  15     "Persisting a workspace path, lock handle, raw git output, remote URL, or arbitrary Git diagnostic in a durable intent, state, receipt, or artifact manifest.",
  16     "Making an advisory local lock substitute for re-observing Git state before effects."
  17   ],
  18   "acceptance_criteria": [
  19     {
  20       "id": "AC-001",
  21       "criterion": "Version-1 authorization starts from a caller-supplied workspace root, canonicalizes that root, discovers the Git repository containing it, and rejects a root that does not resolve to that repository's worktree root. The observed identity is the exact full CommitSha at HEAD; it is never supplied by a CLI flag, inferred from a branch name, or obtained from a remote ref. The private trust evidence binds the canonical root and observed commit together.",
  22       "is_error_case": true
  23     },
  24     {
  25       "id": "AC-002",
  26       "criterion": "Version 1 accepts only a SHA-1 Git repository and a detached HEAD at the exact 40-hex GitCommit SourceIdentity in the received ReleaseIntentV1. It rejects SHA-256 Git-object-format repositories, a symbolic HEAD even when it currently resolves to the same commit, an absent/unresolvable HEAD, a non-canonical or non-equal commit, and a shallow/incomplete checkout when the required commit or tag inspection cannot be performed. Equality uses CommitSha values, never prefix or raw-string comparison.",
  27       "is_error_case": true
  28     },
  29     {
  30       "id": "AC-003",
  31       "criterion": "Authorization requires a clean worktree before the capability is issued. 'Clean' means Git reports no staged, unstaged, unmerged, or untracked file under the repository worktree. An ignored file is clean only when its safe relative path matches Callisto's fixed, versioned harmless-artifact allowlist; arbitrary repository .gitignore rules never grant release-trust authority. A path outside the canonical root, an allowlist mismatch, an error while determining status, or an ambiguous repository layout fails closed. Diagnostics identify the policy condition and safe relative paths where available, but do not retain raw command output in durable data.",
  32       "is_error_case": true
  33     },
  34     {
  35       "id": "AC-004",
  36       "criterion": "A ReleaseWorkspaceLock is acquired after root/repository discovery and held from the final successful authorization observation until the validated capability is dropped after state/receipt persistence. Its lock identity is derived from the canonical workspace root using a stable collision-resistant digest and its lock file is outside the checkout in the platform application-state area (or a caller-selected operational directory). It is an exclusive OS-backed advisory lock, releases on process exit/crash, and reports contention with a stable structured error. The lock path and handle are private operational data, not serializable release data.",
  37       "is_error_case": true
  38     },
  39     {
  40       "id": "AC-005",
  41       "criterion": "The release executor re-observes the same canonical root, detached HEAD, clean-worktree status, and exact approved commit while holding ReleaseWorkspaceLock immediately before every remote or VCS effect. A change after authorization blocks the next effect; the lock only coordinates cooperating Callisto processes and never makes external writers safe by assumption.",
  42       "is_error_case": true
  43     },
  44     {
  45       "id": "AC-006",
  46       "criterion": "The trust API is a read-only callisto-vcs surface returning closed, typed GitCommitTrustEvidence and ReleaseWorkspaceLock values. It does not depend on callisto-graph, callisto-cli, forge SDKs, or registry clients. Its errors derive miette::Diagnostic with stable codes and remediation, and its durable-facing output contains only validated typed identities rather than shell text.",
  47       "is_error_case": false
  48     },
  49     {
  50       "id": "AC-007",
  51       "criterion": "Tests cover non-Git roots, nested/non-root invocation, symbolic HEAD, dirty tracked and untracked worktrees, commit mismatch, lock contention, lock release after drop, and a mutation between authorization and an effect-time recheck. Tests assert that each failure occurs before an effect adapter is invoked.",
  52       "is_error_case": true
  53     }
  54   ],
  55   "implementation_notes": [
  56     "GitAccess/ShellGit should expose structured observation rather than making graph parse porcelain or command text. The existing CommitSha type is the equality boundary.",
  57     "Use a maintained cross-platform file-lock crate only if it provides process-lifetime exclusive locking with explicit acquisition errors. Keep the dependency in callisto-vcs or a lower permitted layer; do not introduce Tokio or Rayon for this ordered, lock-held path.",
  58     "A future closed-root byte observer may add HermeticContent under a separate schema/profile version. It must not weaken the GitCommit behavior specified here."
  59   ],
  60   "reasoning": "A Git commit only becomes a release trust boundary when the executor proves it is operating at the approved checkout and prevents its own concurrent release processes from racing. A local lock improves coordination; mandatory fresh observation preserves correctness when another tool changes the workspace."
  61 }

## .claude/specs/SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013.json
   1 {
   2   "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013",
   3   "status": "draft",
   4   "owner_track": "release-security",
   5   "last_verified_revision": "289001ec",
   6   "depends_on": [
   7     "SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-012"
   8   ],
   9   "purpose": "Expose the release architecture through a clear CLI and portable CI contract, and migrate Callisto's GitHub Actions release workflow to an artifact-bound, Environment-gated execution job without preserving legacy mutation bypasses.",
  10   "scope": "The release CLI command family, legacy-command transition, user-facing state-path and artifact inputs, GitHub Actions plan/build/execute topology, managed release-PR continuity, workflow permissions and action pinning, and documentation needed to operate the new flow. Provider-neutral planning, capability validation, state, and effects are owned by predecessor specs and consumed here.",
  11   "non_goals": [
  12     "Making GitHub Actions the only supported CI provider or moving core release authority into workflow shell scripts.",
  13     "Allowing a command-line flag, environment variable, CI cache, inline JSON, or workflow input to bypass release intent validation, Git trust, artifact verification, or ApplyPermit.",
  14     "Keeping legacy publish/tag mutation behavior indefinitely."
  15   ],
  16   "command_contract": {
  17     "release plan": "Read-only. Local use derives a decision from exact qualified package selections. CI uses an explicit merged-release-commit mode to interpret the immutable parent-to-merged Callisto release-PR delta, verify the consumed changesets and version/changelog closure, and embed the result in a transient intent. It does not rerun changeset planning after merge and it neither publishes, tags, pushes, nor creates a forge release.",
  18     "release inspect": "Read-only. Displays an intent, artifact manifest, state, or receipt with their binding and readiness checks; it does not recompute an unapproved intent as a side effect.",
  19     "release execute": "The sole production mutation entry point. It consumes explicit intent and, when needed, artifact-manifest inputs, validates them, obtains a fresh ValidatedReleaseIntent and ApplyPermit, and runs the coordinator from SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-012.",
  20     "release reconcile": "Read-only. Consumes explicit intent/state inputs and performs exact provider observations to report recoverability; it never publishes, tags, pushes, or creates a forge release."
  21   },
  22   "acceptance_criteria": [
  23     {
  24       "id": "AC-001",
  25       "criterion": "Callisto exposes `release plan`, `release inspect`, `release execute`, and `release reconcile` as explicitly named commands or an equally explicit namespaced interface with the four contracts above. `release plan` requires repeated exact qualified package selections or one named documented configuration-selection mode and embeds the resulting decision in the intent. `release execute` requires an explicit intent file path; it never searches the checkout, falls back to a default plan, accepts an inline JSON authority string, accepts a new selection, or recomputes a plan after validation fails. It accepts an explicit artifact-manifest path when the intent declares binary slots, and an optional explicit state path; omitting the latter uses SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-012's outside-checkout default. Parse, trust, binding, capability, artifact, attestation, or state validation failures exit non-zero before credentials or mutating adapters are reached.",
  26       "is_error_case": true
  27     },
  28     {
  29       "id": "AC-002",
  30       "criterion": "`release plan`, `release inspect`, and `release reconcile` are structurally read-only: their reachable command paths cannot call registry publish, Git tag/push, forge-release creation, or any provider effect adapter. `release execute` is structurally the only production CLI route that can acquire an ApplyPermit and dispatch those adapters. Integration tests invoke every command against recording adapters and assert the exact allowed effect set, including that each error path dispatches none.",
  31       "is_error_case": true
  32     },
  33     {
  34       "id": "AC-003",
  35       "criterion": "During the documented migration window, `plan-publish`, `publish`, `tag --plan`, and `filter-plan` remain available only as clearly labelled read-only compatibility previews. They may render proposed operations but cannot publish, tag, push, write release state, create a forge release, or acquire ApplyPermit. Their help and diagnostics name `release plan`, `release execute`, or `release reconcile` as the replacement as appropriate. A separately documented breaking release removes the legacy commands rather than silently restoring their mutation behavior.",
  36       "is_error_case": true
  37     },
  38     {
  39       "id": "AC-004",
  40       "criterion": "The repository has a separate least-privilege version-PR flow and a GitHub release workflow with separate plan, build, and execute jobs. The version-PR flow recomputes the generated version/changelog/consumed-changeset delta from the current base branch rather than rebasing a prior generated commit; normally it creates or updates one stable managed release PR and removes exactly the consumed changesets only in that PR. The flow updates the managed branch through the forge's commit API rather than a local `git push`, specifically so the built-in token never needs to write `.github/workflows/*` on any ref: it stages the generated change as a commit rooted at the current base via `createCommitOnBranch` on a deterministic staging branch, then moves the managed branch's ref onto that commit with a plain REST ref update. A managed branch already replaced under the prior SHA-suffixed fallback (a `--<sha>` suffix) remains a trusted, ordinary managed branch and continues to be updated in place. This requires no elevated token, never removes changesets from the base branch, and trusts only the canonical managed branch or an exact SHA-suffixed replacement branch from the repository itself. An optional App or fine-grained token may retain the same PR number but is never required for the default flow. The unprivileged release-plan job checks out the exact merged release commit and its parent, proves the reviewed release delta, runs only read-only merged-release-commit planning, and uploads the transient intent file plus its SHA-256 as same-run workflow artifacts. The build job consumes that exact intent, builds the declared binary slots from the matching source commit, verifies its own intent digest, creates a GitHub artifact attestation for each binary with `attestations: write` and `id-token: write` only in that job, and uploads the artifact manifest and binaries as workflow artifacts. The privileged execute job downloads only artifacts from the same workflow run, independently verifies the intent SHA-256, source commit, artifact-manifest bindings, downloaded binary digests, and each binary's GitHub attestation against the configured repository and immutable signer workflow before invoking `release execute`. No decision or intent is committed or recovered from a cache. A plan/build/execute/attestation mismatch fails before registry, Git, or forge credentials are available.",
  41       "is_error_case": true
  42     },
  43     {
  44       "id": "AC-005",
  45       "criterion": "The GitHub execute job is the only job with release secrets or write-scoped token permissions and is bound to a named GitHub Environment with required reviewers and branch/tag deployment rules. Workflow documentation states the environment name and an administrator-verifiable procedure to confirm its live protection rules; a CI/setup check queries GitHub's API and rejects an environment without non-empty required reviewers. Workflow YAML alone is not evidence that the gate is configured. Planning/build jobs use read-only or no token permissions and receive neither registry nor forge credentials.",
  46       "is_error_case": true
  47     },
  48     {
  49       "id": "AC-006",
  50       "criterion": "Every workflow/job declares least-privilege permissions. Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable full commit SHAs with nearby upstream-release comments, and an automated policy check rejects mutable action tags or branches. CODEOWNERS plus branch protection requires designated review for changes under `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/`. Caches may accelerate dependency installation but cannot carry an intent, state, receipt, artifact manifest, artifact bytes, or authority across jobs/runs.",
  51       "is_error_case": true
  52     },
  53     {
  54       "id": "AC-007",
  55       "criterion": "The CLI reference and release-operation documentation provide one end-to-end local and CI recovery flow: create intent from a clean detached checkout; inspect it; build/produce the intent-bound artifact manifest when binaries are declared; execute with an optional explicit state path; reconcile after interruption. Documentation distinguishes source crate publishes from compiled binary uploads, explains that local default state is outside the checkout, and never instructs users to commit state or use GitHub cache for release authority/recovery.",
  56       "is_error_case": false
  57     }
  58   ],
  59   "implementation_notes": [
  60     "The composite action may be retained for non-privileged setup or read-only operations, but it cannot by itself enforce the plan/build/Environment-gated job boundary. The repository workflow must express that boundary.",
  61     "The artifact handoff is transport, not approval. The execute job repeats cryptographic and semantic binding checks in the Callisto CLI before adapter construction. GitHub artifact attestations prove build provenance for the binary bytes; the intent and manifest additionally prove those bytes are the assets this release approved.",
  62     "Other CI providers can implement the same explicit-file contract: immutable intent digest, exact source checkout, manifest-plus-byte verification, state artifact, and a separately protected execute credential boundary."
  63   ],
  64   "revision_note": "Split from umbrella SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-FOUNDATION-007 to keep user/CI entry points and GitHub-specific controls dependent on a settled provider-neutral execution contract. Amended to make the managed release-PR reconstruction contract explicit and to provide a zero-configuration, SHA-suffixed fallback for GitHub's workflow-ref permission restriction.\n\nAmended again after empirical testing against the real orin-dx/callisto public repository showed the SHA-suffixed fallback masked, rather than fixed, GitHub's workflow-permission restriction, causing visible PR churn. AC-004 now describes the forge-commit-API approach (see SPEC-RELEASE-PR-DECISION-014) that avoids the restriction entirely instead of working around it with a replacement branch."
  65 }

  12   "scope": "The provider-neutral execution coordinator, durable state and terminal receipt, state storage, reconciliation, artifact-manifest validation, and provider observation/effect adapter contracts.   14     "Distributed transactions, rollback of a completed registry publication, or parallel remote effects.",
  15     "Publishing, tagging, or creating a forge release from PublishPlan, PublishReport, inline configuration, a cache entry, mutable workspace configuration, or a caller-computed provider target.",
  16     "Persisting credentials, raw registry endpoints, request headers, command lines, provider stderr, arbitrary error text, miette reports, or raw configuration bytes in execution state, receipts, or artifact manifests.",
  17     "Supporting non-Git or non-detached source trust in version 1.",
  18     "Using Rayon or Tokio to parallelize lock-held, ordered release effects."
